candidate.answerReason: The threshold corresponding to 800 individuals is x=10^4. Because the formula counts incomes strictly exceeding x, the lowest income among the wealthiest 800 exceeds this threshold and hence is at least 10^4 dollars.

methods.label: Solve for the threshold of 800 people
methods.explanation:
The relevant threshold is the income \(x\) above which the formula counts \(800\) individuals. For this formula, \(x>0\), and the negative exponent means
\[
800=\frac{8\cdot10^8}{x^{3/2}}.
\]
Multiplying by the positive denominator and dividing by \(800\) gives
\[
x^{3/2}=10^6.
\]
Since \(x^{3/2}=(\sqrt{x})^3\) and \(100^3=10^6\), the unique positive solution is
\[
\sqrt{x}=100,
\qquad x=10000=10^4.
\]
Thus \(800\) individuals have incomes strictly greater than \(10000\) dollars. If \(L\) is the lowest income among the wealthiest \(800\), then \(L>10000\), so certainly \(L\ge10^4\).

To rule out the larger listed bounds, the same formula gives
\[
N(40000)=\frac{8\cdot10^8}{200^3}=100.
\]
Only \(100\) individuals exceed \(40000\) dollars, so \(L\le40000\). Every other listed bound is at least \(10^6\). Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{\text{A, }10^4\text{ dollars}}\).
